meta.request: Score inbound B2B leads from a contact-form submission (name, company, role, message): estimate company size and fit for a developer-tools product, compute a 0-100 lead score with explicit weights, route hot leads to a personalized reply draft and cold leads to a nurture tag.

taskSpec.name: Lead Scorer & Router
taskSpec.summary: Scores inbound B2B contact-form leads 0-100 with transparent weights, estimates company size and developer-tools fit, and routes hot leads to a personalized reply draft or cold leads to a nurture tag.
taskSpec.goal: Given a contact-form submission, produce a scored, routed lead record with an explicit score breakdown and an appropriate next action (personalized reply draft or nurture tag).

inputs.name: lead_name
inputs.description: Full name of the person who submitted the contact form.

inputs.name: company
inputs.description: Company name as entered on the form.

inputs.name: role
inputs.description: Job title or role as entered on the form; may be blank or free-text.

inputs.name: message
inputs.description: Free-text message from the form describing their need or interest.
inputs.example: We're evaluating CI tooling for a team of ~40 devs, hoping to roll out next quarter.

outputs.name: lead_score
outputs.description: Total score from 0-100, sum of weighted component scores.

outputs.name: score_breakdown
outputs.description: Component scores with explicit weights: role_seniority (30), company_size_fit (25), message_intent (25), use_case_fit (20); each component 0-100 scaled by its weight.

outputs.name: company_size_estimate
outputs.description: Estimated engineering team size band (e.g., 1-10, 11-50, 51-200, 200+) with the evidence from the message/role used to justify it.

outputs.name: fit_assessment
outputs.description: Short narrative on how well the lead fits a developer-tools ICP.

outputs.name: reply_draft
outputs.description: Personalized reply email draft referencing the lead's name, company, role, and stated need. Present for hot leads; null otherwise.

outputs.name: nurture_tag
outputs.description: Nurture tag such as 'nurture:early-stage' or 'nurture:non-technical'. Present for cold leads; null otherwise.

steps: Parse the submission and normalize fields (trim whitespace, infer missing role as 'unspecified').
Estimate engineering team size from explicit signals in the message (e.g., 'team of ~40 devs') and role seniority; assign a size band with cited evidence.
Score role_seniority (weight 30): 100 for VP/C-level/Head of, 70 for Director/Principal/Staff, 50 for Senior/Lead, 30 for IC engineer, 10 for student/non-technical/unspecified.
Score company_size_fit (weight 25): 100 for 51-200 engineers, 80 for 11-50, 60 for 200+, 30 for 1-10.
Score message_intent (weight 25): 100 for explicit evaluation/purchase timeline, 70 for active evaluation without timeline, 40 for general interest, 10 for vague or unrelated message.
Score use_case_fit (weight 20): 100 for use case directly matching the product's core capabilities, 50 for adjacent use case, 10 for no discernible fit.
Sum weighted components to produce lead_score (0-100); clamp and round to nearest integer.
For hot leads, write a personalized reply draft referencing name, company, role, and their stated need, with a concrete suggested next step (e.g., a call or trial).
For cold leads, assign a nurture tag reflecting the dominant reason for the low score (e.g., non-technical role, too small, no intent).
Return the full record: score, breakdown, size estimate, fit assessment, route, and the applicable action artifact.
constraints: Score must be reproducible: every component score must be justified by cited evidence from the input fields.
Weights must sum to 100 (30/25/25/20) and be shown in the breakdown.
Never fabricate company facts (headcount, funding) not inferable from the inputs; label estimates as estimates.
Reply drafts must be under 150 words and reference at least two personalized details.
Exactly one action artifact per lead: reply_draft for hot, nurture_tag for cold, neither required for warm (may include a light nurture_tag).
Do not include the lead's email or any PII beyond what was submitted.
successCriteria: lead_score is an integer between 0 and 100 and equals the weighted sum shown in score_breakdown.
score_breakdown lists all four components with their weights and raw component scores.
company_size_estimate includes a size band and quotes the input evidence supporting it.
route matches the stated thresholds (hot >=70, warm 40-69, cold <40).
Hot leads have a reply_draft that mentions the lead's name and at least one detail from their message; cold leads have a nurture_tag.
No output field asserts unverifiable company facts as fact.
assumptions: ICP is a developer-tools product; best-fit buyers are engineering leaders at companies with 11-200 engineers.
Default weights: role_seniority 30, company_size_fit 25, message_intent 25, use_case_fit 20.
No external enrichment (web lookup, CRM append) is performed; scoring relies solely on the four form fields.
Warm leads receive neither a full reply draft nor a mandatory nurture tag; a human reviews them.
Output is a single JSON record per submission, suitable for piping into a CRM or email system.
clarifyingQuestions: Should warm leads (40-69) also receive a reply draft, or only hot leads?
Is there a CRM or routing system (e.g., HubSpot, Slack webhook) the route/action should be delivered to, or is JSON output sufficient?

exampleInputs.message: We're evaluating CI tooling for a team of ~40 devs, hoping to roll out next quarter.
Saw your site, looks cool. What does it cost?
Our platform team of 120 is standardizing on new build tooling this year; your docs look like a match for our monorepo setup.
Please add me to your newsletter.

plan.rationale: Each lead is scored deterministically from cited evidence, then routed by threshold into mutually exclusive branches (hot/warm/cold) with branch-specific artifacts. Scoring uses llm_structured for evidence-cited component scores, code for the exact weighted sum, and a router for threshold branching; the reply draft uses refine since it has an explicit quality bar (<150 words, ≥2 personalized details).

steps.purpose: Normalize fields: trim whitespace on lead_name/company/role/message; infer empty role as 'unspecified'.

From the normalized fields, estimate engineering team size band (1-10, 11-50, 51-200, 200+) with quoted evidence, produce fit_assessment narrative, and score the four components (role_seniority, company_size_fit, message_intent, use_case_fit) each 0-100 with cited evidence from the input. No fabricated company facts; estimates labeled as estimates.

Compute lead_score = round(role_seniority*0.30 + company_size_fit*0.25 + message_intent*0.25 + use_case_fit*0.20), clamp 0-100; build score_breakdown object with weights (30/25/25/20), raw component scores, and weighted contributions.
Deterministic threshold routing: hot if score >= 70, warm if 40-69, cold if < 40. Ports: hot, warm, cold.

For hot leads: draft a personalized reply email referencing lead name, company, role, and stated need, with a concrete next step. Criteria: under 150 words, references at least two personalized details, professional tone, no PII beyond submitted fields.
For cold leads: assign a nurture tag reflecting the dominant reason for the low score (e.g., 'nurture:non-technical', 'nurture:early-stage', 'nurture:no-intent') with a one-line justification.
For warm leads: optionally produce a light nurture tag (or null) summarizing the follow-up angle for human review; no reply draft.

Join branches and build the final record: lead_score, score_breakdown, company_size_estimate, fit_assessment, route, reply_draft (hot only, null otherwise), nurture_tag (cold always; warm optional; null for hot).

plan.output: lead_score (number, from compute_score), score_breakdown (object with four weighted components and evidence, from compute_score/assess), company_size_estimate (band + quoted evidence, from assess), fit_assessment (string, from assess), route ('hot'/'warm'/'cold', from route_lead), reply_draft (refined text from draft_reply for hot leads, null otherwise), nurture_tag (from nurture_tag for cold, warm_note optionally for warm, null for hot).

role_seniority.evidence: Role listed as "VP Engineering", a VP-level title.

company_size_fit.evidence: "team of ~40 devs" maps to the 11-50 band, which scores 80.

message_intent.evidence: "We're evaluating CI tooling" (explicit evaluation) with "hoping to roll out next quarter" (purchase timeline).

use_case_fit.evidence: "evaluating CI tooling" directly matches core developer-tooling capabilities.

output.fit_assessment: Priya is a VP Engineering at a company with an explicitly stated ~40-dev engineering team, squarely within the 11-200 engineer ICP. The message shows an active evaluation with a concrete rollout timeline, indicating strong purchase intent. Overall this is a high-fit lead, though company size sits at the lower end of the ICP band.
